mt1-p007a.context: Do sets ke beech common elements ho to unke Venn diagram mein circles overlap karte hain.
walkthrough: Rectangle = universal set U.
Har set ek circle hai.
Overlap = common elements.

example.q: A = {1, 2, 3}, B = {3, 4}: overlap mein kaun sa element?

mt1-p007b.context: Disjoint sets ka Venn diagram: circles alag, koi overlap nahi.
walkthrough: Dono circles alag rakho.
Overlap nahi = common element nahi.
A ∩ B = φ.

mt1-p008.context: Subset mein ek set dusre ke andar hota hai.
walkthrough: Bada circle = B.
Chhota circle = A, B ke andar.
A ke saare elements B mein hain.

mt1-p009a.context: Union ka Venn diagram: dono sets ka combined area.
walkthrough: Dono circles dekho.
Dono ka poora area shade karo.

mt1-p009b.context: Intersection ka Venn diagram: sirf overlap.
walkthrough: Dono circles ka common hissa dekho.
Sirf overlap shade karo.
Result: A ∩ B = {3, 5}.

mt1-p009c.context: Complement ka Venn diagram: universal set ka wo hissa jo A mein nahi hai.
walkthrough: Rectangle U ko dekho.
Circle A ke bahar ka area shade karo.

mt1-p014a.context: A - B: circle A ka wo hissa jo circle B mein nahi.
walkthrough: Pehle A circle dekho.
B wale overlap ko chhod do.
Bacha hua A ka hissa = A - B.

mt1-p014b.context: B - A: circle B ka wo hissa jo circle A mein nahi.
walkthrough: Pehle B circle dekho.
A wale overlap ko chhod do.
Bacha hua B ka hissa = B - A.

mt1-p015.context: Symmetric difference: dono sets ke sirf ek-ek mein wale elements.
walkthrough: Overlap (common) ko chhod do.
Dono circles ka bacha hua hissa shade karo.
Formula: A Δ B = (A - B) ∪ (B - A).

mt2-p002.context: AND (∧) ka truth table: dono inputs true hon tabhi output true.
walkthrough: 4 rows banao (p, q ke 4 combination).
Har row mein p aur q dekho.
Sirf p = 1 aur q = 1 wali row mein output 1.

mt2-p003a.context: OR (∨) ka truth table: koi ek input true ho to output true.
walkthrough: 4 rows banao.
Dekho: kya p ya q true hai?
Sirf dono false wali row mein output 0.

example.q: p = 0 aur q = 1 par p ∨ q?

mt2-p003b.context: Conditional (→): 'agar p to q'. Ye sirf ek case mein false hai.
walkthrough: p ko hypothesis, q ko conclusion maano.
Sirf p = 1 aur q = 0 wali row false.
Baaki sab rows true.

mt2-p004.context: Biconditional (↔): 'p tab aur sirf tab q'. Dono same hon to true.
walkthrough: Row mein p aur q dekho.
Dono same hon to 1.
Alag hon to 0.

example.q: p = 0 aur q = 0 par p ↔ q?

walkthrough: p aur ~p likho.
Har row mein p ya ~p mein se ek true hai.
Final column sab 1: tautology.
p aur ~p likho.
Dono ek saath true kabhi nahi hote.
Final column sab 0: contradiction.

mt2-p006a.context: Slide Example 1: (p ∨ ~q) → (p ∧ q). Columns step by step banaye.
walkthrough: Pehle ~q likho.
Phir p ∨ ~q aur p ∧ q.
Last column: left true, right false = false.

mt2-p006b.context: Slide Example 4: (p → q) → r. Pehle p → q, phir uska r ke saath conditional.
walkthrough: Pehle p → q likho.
Phir (p → q) aur r ka conditional.
Agar (p → q) = 0 ho to result 1.

mt2-p009a.context: Slide example: A = p → q aur B = ~q → ~p. Dono ki final columns same hain, isliye A ≡ B.
walkthrough: A aur B ki alag columns banao.
Dono columns row by row compare karo.
A ↔ B sab rows mein true: tautology, isliye A ≡ B.

example.q: p = 1, q = 0 par A aur B?

mt2-p011.context: Distributive law: p ∧ (q ∨ r) ≡ (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r). Dono sides ka table compare karo.
walkthrough: q ∨ r banao.
LHS = p ∧ (q ∨ r) banao.
RHS = (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r) banao aur LHS se compare karo.

mt3-p001.context: Matrix ka order rows × columns se batate hain. Element a_ij = row i, column j.

head: Symbol
Matlab
rows: row i aur column j ka element

walkthrough: Pehle rows gino (m), phir columns (n).
Order = m × n.
a_ij mein pehla index row, doosra column.

example.q: 2 rows aur 3 columns wale matrix ka order?

mt3-p002.context: Row, column aur zero matrix: order se pehchano.
walkthrough: Rows gino: 1 row = row matrix.
1 column = column matrix.
Sab elements 0 = zero matrix.

mt3-p003.context: Square matrix ke special types: diagonal, scalar, identity.
walkthrough: Pehle check karo square hai ya nahi.
Diagonal ke bahar sab 0 hain?
Diagonal values barabar hain? Ya sab 1?

mt3-p004.context: Triangular matrix: ek side ke sab entries 0.
walkthrough: Matrix square hai ya nahi, pehle dekho.
Diagonal ke neeche 0 hain? Upper.
Diagonal ke upar 0 hain? Lower.

example.q: Upper triangular mein kya zero hai?
example.a: Diagonal ke neeche ke sab entries.

mt3-p005.context: Symmetric: A = Aᵀ. Transpose mein rows aur columns badalte hain.
walkthrough: A ka transpose likho (rows ↔ columns).
A aur Aᵀ compare karo.
Barabar hain to symmetric.

mt3-p013.context: Slide example: A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]] ke liye A² = I.
walkthrough: A × A banao: row × column.
Har element: row ka sum (product) column se.
Result identity I ke barabar.

mt3-p016.context: 3 × 3 determinant: first row ke saath cofactor expansion. Slide example A = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6], [7, 8, 9]].
walkthrough: Row 1 ke har element ke liye minor nikaalo.
Signs +, −, + lagao.
Teeno terms jod do: |A| = 0 (singular).

mt3-p019.context: Minor matrix: har element ka minor (row aur column hata kar bachi determinant).
walkthrough: Element ki row aur column cover karo.
Bachche 2 × 2 matrix ki determinant nikaalo.
9 values ko same order mein rakho: minor matrix M = [[16, −3, 36], [−7, 9, −26], [−13, 5, −19]].
Har minor ke aage sign lagao (+ − + pattern).
Sign lagane ke baad C₁₂ = −(−3) = 3.
9 values ko C matrix mein rakho.

mt3-p021b.context: Adjoint = cofactor matrix ka transpose: adj(A) = Cᵀ.
walkthrough: Cofactor matrix C lo.
Rows aur columns badlo (transpose).
Ye adjoint hai.

mt3-p026.context: 2 × 2 inverse: A⁻¹ = adj(A)/|A|. Slide example A = [[2, 4], [3, 8]].
walkthrough: Pehle |A| nikaalo. 0 nahi to inverse exist karta hai.
2 × 2 adjoint: diagonal swap, baaki ka sign badlo.
Har element ko |A| se divide karo.
|A| nikaalo: −3 (≠ 0, to inverse exist karta hai).
Cofactor matrix banao (9 cofactors).
Transpose lo: adj(A).
Har element ko |A| = −3 se divide karo.

mt1-p010a.context: Complement: universal set ka wo hissa jo A mein nahi.
walkthrough: U ko rectangle maano.
Circle A ke bahar ka area shade karo.
Bache hue elements likho: A' = {3, 6, 7, 8, 10}.

mt1-p010b.context: Union ka example, slide ke jaisa.
walkthrough: A ke elements likho: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
B ke elements likho: 3, 5, 7, 9.
Dono ko jodo, duplicates hatao.

mt1-p011.context: Intersection ka example, slide ke jaisa.
walkthrough: A aur B ke common elements dhoondo.
Sirf overlap shade karo.
Result: {3, 5}.
Har element dekho: kis set mein hai?
Ek element ek hi region mein jata hai.
Jo kisi set mein nahi, wo bahar hai.

example.a: B ∩ C (sirf B aur C dono mein).

mt1-p017r.context: Slide p016–p018: U = factors of 48, A = factors of 24, B = factors of 12, C = factors of 8.
walkthrough: Har divisor ke liye dekho: A, B, C mein se kaun sa?
16 aur 48 kisi set mein nahi (U mein hain).
Sets ke union/intersection ke liye regions se padho.

example.q: A ∪ B aur A ∩ B kya hai?

venn3.caption: U = factors of 48, A = factors of 24, B = factors of 12, C = factors of 8.

walkthrough: Har element ka region dekho.
18 A, B, C teeno mein hai.
Jo kisi mein nahi, wo bahar.

mt2-p006c.context: Slide Example 2 (pehle 'do it yourself' tha). p aur q ke 4 rows.
walkthrough: ~p aur ~q likho.
~p ∧ ~q aur p ∨ q banao.
Last column: left → right.

mt2-p006d.context: Slide Example 3: (i) p ∨ q ∨ r, (ii) p ∧ q ∧ r.
walkthrough: 8 rows (pqr 000 se 111).
OR: koi ek 1 ho to 1.
AND: sab 1 ho to 1 (sirf 111).

example.q: p=1, q=0, r=0 par p ∧ q ∧ r?

walkthrough: ~p likho.
~p → q likho.
~r likho.
Last: (~p → q) → ~r.
~p ∧ q likho.
Phir → r lagao.
Sirf (~p ∧ q) = 1 aur r = 0 par 0.
p ∨ ~q likho.
~r likho.
AND karo, phir NOT (~) lagao.
~(p ∨ q) likho.
~q ∨ r likho.
Last column sab 1 hai, isliye tautology.
~p ∧ q likho.
~r ∧ q likho.
OR karo.
A ki row 1 ko B ki column 1 se multiply karo.
Har element = row × column ka sum.
Result 3 × 3 matrix.
Check: A ke columns = B ke rows (2 = 2).
Result order: 3 × 4.
Har element row × column se.
Order check: 3 × 2 aur 2 × 3 → 3 × 3.
Row × column se har element.
Result 3 × 3.
Row × column.
AB aur BA alag order ke hain.
Har element ka cofactor nikaalo.
Cofactor matrix C banao.
Transpose karo: adj(A) = Cᵀ.
|A| = 15 (≠ 0), inverse exist karta hai.
adj(A) nikaalo.
Har element ko 15 se divide karo.
Cofactor matrix banao.
Transpose karo.
Result adj(A).

mt1-p019a.context: Slide p019: A ∪ B shade, A ∩ B = φ (circles overlap nahi karte).
walkthrough: A aur B alag circles hain.
Dono circle ka area shade karo: union.
Koi overlap nahi, isliye A ∩ B = φ.

mt1-p020.context: Slide p020: A Δ B = (A − B) ∪ (B − A) = A ∪ B.
walkthrough: A − B = A (koi element nahi katta).
B − A = B.
Union: A Δ B = A ∪ B.

mt4-p001.context: A × B = sab ordered pairs (x, y) jahan x ∈ A aur y ∈ B. A = {1, 2, 4}, B = {1, 3, 9}.
walkthrough: A ke har element (row) ko B ke har element (column) ke saath pair karo.
3 × 3 = 9 pairs banenge.
B × A ke liye pair ka order ulta hoga: (1, 1), (1, 2), ...

example.q: A = {1, 2, 4} aur B = {1, 3, 9} ho to n(A × B) kitna hai?

mt4-p002.context: Relation R ⊆ A × B. Pehle A × B likho, phir condition lagao. Example 1: A = {1, 2, 3}, B = {3, 5, 6, 7}, R = {(a, b) | a = b} = {(3, 3)}. Example 2: A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, B = {2, 4, 5, 6}, R = {(a, b) | a > b} = {(3, 2), (4, 2)}.
walkthrough: Pehle A × B ki list banao.
Har pair par condition check karo (a = b, a > b, a + b < 8, ...).
Jo pairs condition pass karein, woh R mein jaate hain.

mt4-p003.context: Domain = pehle elements; Range = dusre elements. Mapping: R = {(1, 5), (2, 8), (3, 12), (4, 7)}, har pair ka ek arrow. Slide ka dusra example: R = {(a, b) | a ≠ b} on A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, B = {3, 4, 5, 6}: domain {1, 2, 3, 4}, range {3, 4, 5, 6}.
walkthrough: Bayi oval = A, daayi oval = B.
Har pair (a, b) ke liye a se b tak arrow.
Jis B element par arrow nahi laga (jaise 17), woh range mein nahi aata.
Rows = A ke elements (3, 5, 7, 11).
Columns = B ke elements (1, 3, 6, 8, 9).
Jo pair R mein hai uske liye 1, warna 0. Jaise (3, 6) ∈ R, isliye row 3, column 6 par 1.

example.q: Row 7 mein 1 kin columns mein hai?

walkthrough: Har a ke liye dekho kaun se b ke liye a + b < 8.
a = 5 aur 6 ke liye koi b nahi, isliye unki rows zero hain.

example.q: Row 2 mein kaun se columns 1 hain?

walkthrough: Pehle A × A likho (n × n pairs).
Condition wale pairs chuno.
Slide ke reflexive example mein R = {(1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 2), (3, 4), (3, 3), (4, 1), (4, 2), (4, 4)} har (a, a) mein hai, isliye reflexive hai.

example.q: A = {1, 2, 3} par R = {(a, b) | a = b} likho.

mt4-p007.context: Reflexive matlab har a ke liye (a, a) ∈ R. Slide mein R ka pehla example: (3, 3) ∉ R, isliye reflexive nahi. Slide ke dusre example mein (2, 2) ∈ R likha hai, lekin 2 + 2 = 4 > 5 nahi hai, isliye (2, 2) ∉ R. Conclusion phir bhi same hai: reflexive nahi.
walkthrough: Har a ∈ A ke liye (a, a) check karo.
Pehla fail hone wala pair kaafi hai — (3, 3) ∉ R.
Dusre example mein condition a + b > 5 hai: a = 2 par 2 + 2 = 4 > 5 false hai.

example.q: A = {2, 3, 4, 5}, R = {(a, b) | a + b > 5}: reflexive hai?

mt4-p008.context: Irreflexive = koi bhi (a, a) ∈ R nahi. Neither example: A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, R = {(a, b) | a + b = 2} = {(1, 1)}. (1, 1) ∈ R, isliye irreflexive nahi; (2, 2) ∉ R, isliye reflexive nahi.
walkthrough: Har a ke liye (a, a) check karo.
Agar sab (a, a) ∉ R, to irreflexive.
Agar kuch (a, a) ∈ R aur kuch ∉ R, to neither.
Har pair (a, b) ka reverse (b, a) check karo.
Ek bhi reverse missing ho to symmetric nahi.
Slide ke a + b < 6 example mein (1, 3) ↔ (3, 1), (2, 3) ↔ (3, 2) sab present hain, isliye symmetric.

mt4-p010.context: Anti-symmetric: (a, b) ∈ R aur a ≠ b ⇒ (b, a) ∉ R. A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, R = {(1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 4), (2, 3), (3, 4)} anti-symmetric hai. a < b on {1, ..., 5} irreflexive hai aur symmetric nahi.
walkthrough: Har pair (a, b) mein a ≠ b ke liye reverse check karo.
Yahi check x > y, x < y aur a + b divisible by 2 par karna (do it yourself).

mt4-p011.context: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, R = {(a, b) | a + b divisible by 3} = {(1, 2), (1, 5), (2, 1), (2, 4), (3, 3), (4, 2), (4, 5), (5, 1), (5, 4)}. Slide ka conclusion: sirf symmetric hai. Transitive definition aur A = {1, 2, 3} par ek example bhi.
walkthrough: Reflexive: (1, 1) ∉ R (1 + 1 = 2), isliye reflexive nahi.
Irreflexive nahi: (3, 3) ∈ R.
Symmetric: har pair ka reverse R mein hai.
Anti-symmetric nahi: (1, 2) aur (2, 1) dono R mein hain.

mt4-p012.context: Transitive: (a, b) ∈ R aur (b, c) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R. Example: R = {(1, 2), (2, 1), (1, 1), (1, 3), (3, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (1, 4), (4, 3)}: (3, 2) aur (2, 3) ∈ R, lekin (3, 3) ∉ R, isliye transitive nahi. Compatibility = reflexive + symmetric; x + y even on {1, ..., 5} ek compatibility relation hai.
walkthrough: Chains dekho: (a, b) aur (b, c) se (a, c) check karo.
Compatibility ke liye sirf reflexive aur symmetric check karo.
x + y even: har (a, a) (2a even), aur (1, 3)/(3, 1) jaise pairs symmetric.
Reflexive: har (a, a) R mein hai.
Transitive: (1, 3) aur (3, 5) se (1, 5) ∈ R; (2, 4) aur (4, 2) se (2, 2) ∈ R. Sab combinations check karo.

example.q: Every equivalence relation compatibility relation hai — True ya False?
example.a: True (equivalence = reflexive + symmetric + transitive, isliye reflexive aur symmetric dono hain).

mt4-p014.context: A = {1, ..., 6}, R = {(x, y) | x + y odd}: reflexive nahi, kyunki (1, 1): 1 + 1 = 2 even. A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, R = {(x, y) | x + y ≤ 8}: slide mein transitive check hota hai; har chain (a, b), (b, c) ke liye (a, c) R mein milta hai.
walkthrough: Pehle reflexive check karo: (1, 1) ∈ R?
Agar nahi, to equivalence nahi — aage check ki zaroorat nahi.
x + y ≤ 8 ke liye symmetric check: x + y = y + x, isliye symmetric.
Transitive: a, c ≤ 4 hone par a + c ≤ 8 hamesha, isliye transitive.

example.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par R = {(x, y) | x + y ≤ 8} equivalence hai?
example.a: Haan — reflexive (2x ≤ 8), symmetric, aur transitive sab satisfy hote hain.

mt4-p015.context: POSET = reflexive + antisymmetric + transitive. A = {1, ..., 5}, R = {(x, y) | x ≤ y}. Slide ke according: reflexive (har (a, a) ∈ R), antisymmetric ((1, 2) ∈ R lekin (2, 1) ∉ R), transitive ((1, 2), (2, 3) ⇒ (1, 3)). Isliye POSET hai.
walkthrough: Reflexive: 1 ≤ 1, 2 ≤ 2, ... sab.
Antisymmetric: (a, b) aur (b, a) dono R mein sirf a = b hone par.
Transitive: (a, b) aur (b, c) ⇒ (a, c) — chain check karo.

example.q: x ≤ y on A = {1, ..., 5} POSET hai?

mt4-p016.context: A = {1, ..., 6}, R = {(x, y) | x = y}: reflexive (1, 1), (2, 2), ... ∈ R; antisymmetric (koi a ≠ b pair nahi); transitive (sirf (a, a) pairs, isliye chain (a, a), (a, a) ⇒ (a, a)). Isliye POSET hai.
walkthrough: Reflexive: har (a, a) R mein hai.
Antisymmetric: (2, 1) ∈ R? Nahi — R mein sirf (a, a) pairs hain.
Transitive: (a, a) aur (a, a) se (a, a) — hamesha satisfy.

example.q: R = {(x, y) | x = y} on {1, ..., 6} POSET hai?

mt4-p017.context: A = {1, ..., 5}, R = {(x, y) | x > y}: reflexive nahi (1 > 1 false), isliye POSET nahi. Function: A se B tak relation jahan har x ∈ A ka exactly ek y ∈ B hai. Example: f: N → N, f(x) = x + 2: f(1) = 3, f(2) = 4, ... function hai.
walkthrough: POSET check: reflexive pehle check karo — x > x kabhi true nahi.
Function check: har input ka exactly ek output.
f(x) = x + 2 ke liye har natural number ka output N mein hai.

example.q: f(x) = x + 2 on N function hai?
example.a: Haan, har x ka exactly ek image hai.

mt4-p018.context: f: A → B, A = {1, 3, 5}, B = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13}, f(x) = 2x + 1: f(1) = 3, f(3) = 7, f(5) = 11, sab B mein hain — function. f: N → N, f(x) = 1 − x: f(1) = 0, f(2) = −1 — N mein nahi, isliye function nahi.
walkthrough: Har input ko rule mein daalo.
Check karo output co-domain B ke andar hai ya nahi.
Composition: (g ∘ f)(x) = g(f(x)). f = x², g = x + 2 par (g ∘ f)(x) = x² + 2 aur (f ∘ g)(x) = (x + 2)².

example.q: f(x) = 1 − x, f: N → N function hai?
example.a: Nahi, f(1) = 0 aur f(2) = −1 N mein nahi hain.

walkthrough: Inner function pehle substitute karo.
Jaise (f ∘ g)(x): g(x) = 3x − 4 ko f mein daalo: 3x − 4 + 3 = 3x − 1.
Composition ka order badalne se answer badalta hai (f ∘ g ≠ g ∘ f).
Teen functions ke composition mein sabse andar wale function se shuru karo.
(f ∘ g ∘ h)(x): pehle h(x) = (x + 2)/3, phir g, phir f.
Bijective check: f, g, h sab linear hain aur R → R par one-one aur onto hain, isliye bijective.
